paper.title: BISTRO: An Efficient Relaxation-Based Method for Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with i.i.d. covariates and arbitrary costs (hybrid i.i.d.-adversarial)
unmapped: learner can sample future contexts from P_x (unlabeled data)
arbitrary (possibly uncountable) policy class F with value-of-ERM oracle access
settings.definition_quote: We assume that $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are drawn i.i.d. from some unknown distribution $P_x$ on $\X$. At the same time, we do not place any assumption on the sequence of costs $c_1,\ldots,c_n$, which may evolve according to some arbitrary stochastic process, or be an ``individual sequence,'' or even be chosen adaptively and adversarially.

unmapped: requires an admissible full-information relaxation for the policy class
settings.definition_quote: Suppose we place no assumption on the evolution of $x_t$'s, which may now be treated as worst-case.

algorithms.name: Bandit reduction of full-information relaxation (uniform mixing with importance-weighted estimates)

symbols.Rad_F: expected vector-valued Rademacher average E Rad(F; x_{1:n}) of the policy class on n i.i.d. contexts

conditions: contexts i.i.d. from P_x and learner can draw samples from P_x

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: The partial-information relaxation ... is admissible. An admissible randomized strategy for this relaxation is given by BISTRO (Algorithm~\ref{alg}). The expected regret of the algorithm with $\gamma=\sqrt{2\En\Rad(\F;x_{1:n})/(nd)}$ is upper bounded by $$2\sqrt{2d \cdot n \cdot \En\Rad(\F;x_{1:n})}.$$

results.notes: Paper's d = number of actions (K), n = T. Polynomial per round given a value-of-ERM oracle (d calls per round). For finite F the intro states this gives O(n^{3/4}(log|F|)^{1/4}). Data-dependent classes: Rad replaced by Rad(F[x_{1:n}]).

symbols.Rad_Mtilde: expected Rademacher average of the relaxed superset of matrices tilde M containing the policy matrices

conditions: tilde M superset of policy matrices with column sums <= 1
tuning: ERM computed over relaxed set tilde M (e.g. LP relaxation)

source.label: lem:opt_relaxation
source.quote: Let $\widetilde{\cM}\supseteq\Mhat$ be a set of matrices such that the column sum $\sum_{j=1}^d M_t(j) \leq 1$ ... BISTRO (with ERM over $\widetilde{\cM}$ rather than $\cM$) is an admissible strategy for this relaxation and the expected regret is upper bounded by $$2\sqrt{2d\cdot n\cdot \En\Rad(\widetilde{\cM})}.$$

results.notes: gamma tuning implicitly analogous to Theorem 2. Regret still against the original class F.

symbols.Rel_full: initial value of an admissible full-information relaxation Rel^dagger(emptyset) for the policy class

conditions: an admissible full-information relaxation exists for F
tuning: q_t=(1-d gamma)q_t^* + gamma 1 with gamma optimized

source.label: lem:if_full_then_partial
source.quote: If $\Relfull{}{}$ is an admissible full-information relaxation for the adversarial scenario, then $$\Rel{}{I_{1:t}} \deq \gamma^{-1}\Relfull{}{\gamma\tilde{c}_{1},\ldots,\gamma\tilde{c}_t}+(n-t)d\gamma$$ is admissible ... The resulting regret upper bound is $$2\sqrt{d \cdot n \cdot \Relfull{}{\emptyset}}.$$

results.notes: Time complexity equals that of the full-information procedure. Generic reduction; adversary type taken as adaptive per admissibility definition but unbiased-estimate argument suggests oblivious costs.
